frameworks.name: Happiness vs. Satisfaction Framework
frameworks.definition: A distinction between contentment with present work and action-oriented dissatisfaction; the model requires remaining happy with the process while maintaining strategic dissatisfaction with the outcome to sustain effort.

claims.text: Hard work is the goal, not a means to an outcome; the result or consequence of hard work is secondary (Alex Hormozi, MoreMozi clip channel).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: A person can be happy but not satisfied — content with their work without complacency. Satisfaction means ceasing to take action; happiness allows action to continue.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: When Hormozi did not work, he was bored and felt depressed; when he works, he is stressed but experiences genuine enjoyment. Therefore, hard work is preferable to inaction despite stress.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Work enables moments of genuine enjoyment and usefulness that inaction cannot provide.
bounded_by: Does not apply to individuals whose primary motivation source is leisure or avoidance of stress.

claims.text: There is misery on both sides of the work/non-work choice; given this equivalence, productivity and usefulness justify choosing work.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: A Haitian proverb states: 'Behind mountains are more mountains.' After every peak is reached, additional peaks appear ahead, framing the journey as perpetual.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: The work works on you more than you work on it; hard work shapes the person undertaking it more deeply than the person shapes the work.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Only by remaining happy about the process but not satisfied with the outcome can a person continue to provide value to the world.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Desire to provide continuous value to others
claims.mechanism: Satisfaction creates complacency and action cessation; happiness maintains effort while dissatisfaction sustains improvement.

claims.text: Hormozi's 10-stage business roadmap applies uniformly across software, physical products, service businesses, and brick-and-mortar retail; less than 1% of companies complete all stages.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Any business model (software, product, service, brick-and-mortar)

numbers.axis: Percentage of companies completing full 10-stage roadmap

examples.text: Hormozi recalls a year when he entered partial retirement to determine his life direction. Through that reflection period, he developed the thesis that hard work itself is the goal—not merely the vehicle to achieve an external outcome. This realization became foundational to his subsequent business philosophy.

When a friend asked Hormozi why he still works despite his success, he answered: 'Because it is the thing I enjoy doing most.' Upon reflection, he observed that periods without work produced boredom and depression, while periods of intensive work produced stress but also genuine moments of enjoyment. This comparison led him to conclude that productivity justifies accepting the accompanying stress.

practices.text: To access Hormozi's 10-stage business roadmap template, visit acquisition.com/roadmap, enter your information, and download the free resource that breaks each stage into eight business functions.
Maintain happiness with your daily work and process while preserving strategic dissatisfaction with current outcomes to drive continued improvement and value creation.
